F_122.py.description: F-122: make fe_arm engage idempotent. Adds test_bit(fe_port_armed) check at top of __fman_pcd_fe_arm_engage() (shared core, protects both debugfs and API paths) returning 0 with pr_info when already engaged. Also changes F-107 -EBUSY guard in fman_pcd_fe_engage() to idempotent return 0. Runs before F-125/F-126.

F_125.py.description: F-125: make FE-VM engage transactional. __fman_pcd_fe_arm_engage() returned on kg_port_arm_fe failure with pcd->fe_scaffold_* still set; the next attempt overwrote those fields, orphaning the 304-byte FE_ENTER scaffold (gro 256 + mto 16 + ato 32) permanently. Measured at exactly 304 B per failed engage on .185 and .106, reclaimable only by reboot, and the source of the arena fragmentation that made even single-port engage fail -ENOMEM. Also unwinds a partial 3-way allocation. Reuses the existing fman_pcd_fe_arm_free_scaffold(). Runs after F-118.

F_128.py.description: F-128: F-125(c) — free ehash on LAST port disengage. Changes F_092's teardown guard from fe_vm_chain_built to fe_vm_chain_built && list_empty(&pcd->fe_ports). The shared FE-VM chain is torn down only when the last port disengages, returning 33280 B MURAM (int_buf) + 512 KiB DDR (bucket table). Runs after F-092.

F_129.py.description: F-129: add FE-VM chain teardown to production fman_pcd_fe_disengage(). F_092 inserted teardown into the DEBUGFS handler only; the production YNL/genl path had ZERO teardown. Board-verified 2026-07-27: disengage leaves ehash int_buf refcount=1, 33280 B held. Inserts teardown with list_empty guard after __fman_pcd_fe_arm_disengage() in the production function. Runs after F-128.

F_130.py.description: F-130: grow PCD MURAM arena 64 KiB -> 84 KiB. The ehash int_buf (33280 B) + two per-port pools (~9029 B each) = 51338 B fits by total bytes but fails on placement because the int_buf at offset 0x4c100 fragments the arena. Contiguous MURAM extent 0x4ac00->0x60000 = 86016 B (84 KiB). Must run BEFORE F-092 (VM chain build) so gen_pool is sized before any allocation.

active.F_167.py: fman_pcd.c: F-167 — standalone FMFP_EXTC (FPM External Requests Control, CCSR 0x074) SYNC probe. DPAA RM §5.12.14.1 documents this register's INV0 bit as required by all three officially-documented Custom Classifier table update flows; fman_pcd_ehash_add_key() has never asserted it -- a candidate for both the ehash MISS and the AC_CC/FE_ENTER port-wedge. Adds an inert-by-default debugfs node (fe_extc: cat reads the register, 'echo sync' asserts INV0 and polls for HW to clear it) so the register can be tested standalone without engaging any port. Purely additive; does not touch fman_pcd_ehash_add_key() or any existing fe_* code path.
active.F_168.py: fman_port.c: F-168 — wires a real FMFP_EXTC SYNC assertion into fman_port_set_cc_base(), between the fmbm_rccb write (repoints the AC_CC dispatch target) and the fmbm_rfpne write (enables dispatch into it). F-167 board-confirmed the register is safe/responsive to touch standalone (echo sync > fe_extc on .185, zero adverse effect, repeated twice); F-168 is the first test with an actual port arm in the picture, testing whether SYNC prevents the port-wedge that has reproducibly occurred on every prior AC_CC arm attempt this session. active.F_169.py: fman_pcd.c: F-169 — debugfs verb (fe_kg_ekfc: 'set <scheme_id_hex> <ekfc_hex>') to reconfigure a live KeyGen scheme's EKFC. T-M3-R attempt 1 (genuine ehash HIT test) stalled with a real harness gap found: KeyGen scheme4 was never reconfigured off its own 12-byte CC-tree EKFC (0x00180006) to match the 14-byte ehash table's format (F-163's 0x801C0006) before the FE_ENTER-direct arm. The existing fman_pcd_kg_scheme_set_ekfc() (fman_pcd_kg.c) has zero callers because it's buggy -- a single enable=true call against an already-bound scheme is rejected by keygen_scheme_setup()'s own used-scheme guard. F-169 implements the correct disable/mutate/re-enable sequence fresh, directly against fman->keygen->schemes[] via the module-internal fman_keygen_internal.h (designed for exactly this kind of sibling-translation-unit access). Purely additive; only fires on an explicit set write, intended to run immediately before fe_arm engage.
active.F_171.py: fman_pcd.c: F-171 — adds a `fe_group` debugfs verb that wraps the existing FE_ENTER chain (built by `fe_enter build`) in a genuine CONT_LOOKUP group AD (RM §8.7.4.1/§7.11: numKeys=1, matchTableAddr, adTableAddr, keySize=16) with an all-wildcard match row (mask=0x00 on every byte), instead of writing FE_ENTER directly to FMBM_RCCB as every off!=0 T-M3-R arm this session has done — the deprecated 'RCCB→FE_ENTER direct' topology the RM says was superseded 2026-07-16. The all-wildcard mask sidesteps F-158's still-open CC-compare-window-layout question entirely: any frame reaching this group AD trivially matches regardless of byte order, and dispatches into the already-built, already-byte-verified FE_ENTER chain. `echo "build <miss_fqid_hex>" > fe_group` builds match table (64B) + AD table (32B, ato[0]=verbatim copy of fe_enter's root AD, ato[1]=miss-AD) + the 16B group AD itself; `cat fe_group` shows the group AD's own offset, which is what gets passed to the existing `fe_arm engage <port> <offset> <fqid>` instead of fe_enter's own root_ad offset. Purely additive; fe_arm itself is unmodified.
active.F_172.py: fman_pcd.c: F-172 — extends F-171's `fe_group` write handler to accept an explicit 16-byte key + 16-byte mask (`echo "build <miss_fqid_hex> <32-hex key> <32-hex mask>" > fe_group`), instead of always programming the all-wildcard match row F-171 hardcoded. Motivation: F-171's wildcard test armed cleanly but a discriminator test proved it does not distinguish HIT from MISS (ping and the matching SYN both dispatched to the same FQID regardless of match). Documentation review found the only prior real-key test of this dispatch shape, F-158 (2026-08-01, real key + full participate-mask via `cc_test`, decisive-negative result), predates F-168's FMFP_EXTC SYNC fix (2026-08-06, board-confirmed to fix a real dispatch defect) — so a real key + real mask has never been tried with F-168 present. Adds `fman_pcd_fe_group_hex2bin()` (self-contained hex parser, no kernel hex2bin() dependency) and widens `fman_pcd_fe_group_build()`'s signature to `(pcd, miss_fqid, key, mask)`; `key`/`mask` NULL reproduces F-171's original wildcard default exactly (fully backward compatible). Purely additive on top of F-171; no other fe_* verb or struct field touched.
active.F_173.py: fman_pcd.c: F-173 — adds `wmb()` immediately before `fman_pcd_ehash_add_key()`'s bucket-head-pointer publish (`*flow->bucket_h = swab64(rec_phys)`). A deep read of vendor's own original, unmodified source (github.com/we-are-mono/ASK) found their `fix/security-hardening` branch fixing this project's exact symptom class ("byte-verified-correct key/chain, never a genuine hardware HIT") via an explicit `wmb()` at this exact point, with the rationale that on weak-ordered ARM64 the flow record's own field writes (header, key, next-FE pointer) can still be in the CPU's store buffer when the separate bucket-head pointer write becomes visible to FMan's independent DMA-capable hash-table walker — the walker can then dereference a still-stale record. F-142 (2026-07-30) already fixed the adjacent cache-coherency half of this bug class (kzalloc → dma_alloc_coherent) but never added the write-ordering half; both are independently required. Purely additive — no other fe_* verb, struct field, or write path touched.
active.F_175.py: fman_pcd.c: F-175 — implements a per-flow FE CONTEXT buffer and corrects `ENQ`'s NIA encoding, per a 2026-07-15 finding that this branch only ever implemented layer one of NXP's real two-layer FE-VM design (static singleton FEs + a per-flow context, auto-loaded by hardware into the frame's transient workspace on a genuine HIT). An earlier fixup (F-057) had already removed an inline trailing-bytes write at this same location after finding it corrupts the ehash record; reading the actual SDK oracle source directly (the real, non-stub `FmPcdCcBuildContextByFE()`/`ExternalHashTableAddKey()`) resolves the disagreement — the FE context is a SEPARATELY allocated 16B DMA buffer (only `MUX`+`ENQ` needed, no HM/replication chain in this branch), never inline in the record; the record instead carries an 8-byte DMA pointer to it (matching the SDK's `t_FmExtHashResult.contex_addr` width). F-057's fix was correct for that location; this fixup's field encoding (`MUX`@0 = ENQ's MURAM offset, `ENQ`@8/12 = `(rspid<<24)|fqid` / `ppid<<16`) is now validated byte-exact against the real SDK encoder. Also corrects `fman_pcd_fe_enq_build()` to the vendor/board-tested encoding (`ws_offset=8`, `NIA_ENG_BMI|NIA_BMI_AC_ENQ_FRAME=0x00500002` in word1 instead of a raw FQID, chains to `EXIT`) — tried on silicon 2026-07-16 (F-073B), got one frame through before stopping. Adds `ctx`/`ctx_dma` fields to `struct fman_pcd_ehash_flow`, freed alongside the record on drain. `fe_enq`'s debugfs `build` verb drops its fqid argument (ENQ is now a plain singleton); `fe_flow add`'s third argument changes role from an ENQ FE MURAM offset to the target FQID. Updates both call sites sharing `fman_pcd_ehash_add_key()` (the `fe_flow` debugfs path and the `ask.ko`-facing kernel API `fman_pcd_fe_flow_add()`, retyped by F-094) so the build stays consistent — the public `fman_pcd_fe_flow_action.enq_off` field is reinterpreted as the FQID rather than renamed, avoiding a second breaking header change on top of F-094's.
active.F_176.py: fman_pcd.c: F-176 adds a dispatch/FQID-independent HIT discriminator (new debugfs node fe_ehash_stats). Phase 1 of plans/EHASH-DUAL-FIX-VERIFICATION-PLAN.md, following Phase 0's CORRECTED verdict (2026-08-07): a first pass misread the wrong vendor function family (ext_hash_add_key()/t_FmPcdCcNodeExtHashInfo, reachable only via FM_PCD_HashTableSet(), never called by cdx_ehash.c) and wrongly concluded the ehash bucket/record format needed a structural rewrite; retracted same day after checking the function cdx_ehash.c actually calls (ExternalHashTableAddKey()/en_exthash_bucket/en_exthash_node/en_ehash_entry) -- this project's format is bit-exact correct, no rewrite needed. Genuinely new: en_ehash_entry's second union view exposes hardware-writeback packet_count/packet_bytes/timestamp counters (320B entries, SET_STATS_ENABLE/SET_TIMESTAMP_ENABLE flag bits) -- enabled unconditionally here, readable via the new debugfs node, giving the first way to confirm hardware performed a compare independent of FQID/dispatch outcome.
active.F_177.py: fman_pcd.c: F-177, T-M3-R Phase 2 item 2 (2026-08-07). Phase 1 (F-176 corrected to STATS_EN-only) confirmed the FE-VM ehash zero-HIT result is real. Phase 2 item 1 (byte-for-byte re-check of en_exthash_node.word_1's int_buf_pool_addr/global_mem_offset against vendor's real ExternalHashTableSet()/FM_PCD_Init()) found this project's encoding already bit-exact correct -- closed, no fix. Item 2 (this fixup): F-168 wired an FMFP_EXTC[INV0] SYNC assertion into fman_port_set_cc_base()'s FMBM_RCCB write (RM S5.12.14.1: required after changing a live FMan-controller-walked structure before dispatch into it is safe) and it fixed the historical port-wedge on arm. The ehash bucket table is exactly such a structure, yet fman_pcd_ehash_add_key()'s own bucket-head publish (F-173's wmb()-then-swab64() sequence) has never asserted it. F-177 adds the same SYNC there, on both call sites sharing fman_pcd_ehash_add_key() (the fe_flow debugfs path and the ask.ko-facing fman_pcd_fe_flow_add() API, per F-175's precedent). Weaker hypothesis than F-168's own (vendor's real ExternalHashTableAddKey() fast-insert path calls no sync of any kind), but cheap, additive-only (best-effort: logs a timeout, does not fail the insert), and the last concrete insert-path lead before Phase 3.
active.F_178.py: fman_pcd_kg.c: F-178 (2026-08-07), written in direct response to the user's challenge: vendor's real ASK code demonstrably works on this exact board/microcode, so what does this project's own approach do differently? Full read of vendor's real FM_PORT_SetPCD()/SetPcd() documents that for a single-bound-scheme port, vendor ALWAYS ORs NIA_KG_DIRECT | physicalSchemeId into fmbm_rfpne -- without it, KeyGen falls back to the generic SI/match-vector walk (RM sec 4.4) instead of deterministically dispatching to the CC-attached scheme. F-162 (2026-08-05) already found and fixed exactly this gap once, but wired the fix ONLY into fman_pcd_kg_port_attach_cc()/detach_cc() -- the CONT_LOOKUP/group-AD 'CC-graft' mechanism this project's own history has since abandoned. The ACTUAL arm path every T-M3-R test has ever used, fman_pcd_kg_port_arm_fe()/_disarm_fe() (patch 0132), is a separate function pair that reprograms the scheme's next_engine and calls fman_port_set_cc_base(), but NEVER calls F-162's own fman_port_set_kg_direct_scheme() helper -- confirmed directly by this session's own dmesg on every single arm ('rfpne 0x00480200', never '... | NIA_KG_DIRECT | scheme_id'). This means every carefully-configured EKFC/key-format/hash_bytes_offset/PORT_ID value this project has tested on 'scheme 4' may never have actually been consulted for live traffic, if the generic SI/match-vector walk selects a different scheme (or none) instead. Fix: call fman_port_set_kg_direct_scheme(rxport, id) (F-162's existing, already-CI-wired helper -- id already in scope via kg_find_port_scheme()) at the end of arm_fe()'s success path, symmetric fman_port_clear_kg_direct_scheme(rxport) in disarm_fe(). No new register-level code -- two new call sites reusing F-162's own verified mechanism. Dry-run tested (including idempotency) against the exact reconstructed source text before commit.
active.F_179.py: fman_keygen.c: F-179 (2026-08-07), follow-up while resolving <combine>/PORT_ID against vendor's real, pristine FMC compiler source (github.com/nxp-qoriq/fmc @ 5b9f4b16a864e9dfa58cdcc860be278a7f66ac18, the exact commit this project's own fmc_git.bb pins). That trace definitively found <combine> builds KeyGen's extractedOrs (FQID-only), correcting an earlier doc claim it was a GEC key mechanism -- and while closing out that context, found KG_SCH_KN_PORT_ID (EKFC bit 31, the real key-extraction path, unrelated to <combine>) draws its value from kgse_dv0/kgse_dv1 (fm_pcd_ext.h's t_FmPcdExtractEntry has no dedicated union member for PORT_PRIVATE_INFO; vendor's fm_kg.c BuildSchemeRegs() assigns kgse_dv0/dv1 straight from the scheme's privateDflt0/1 fields). This project's own fman_keygen.c (mainline-derived, unmodified for this logic) populates kgse_dv0/dv1 with DEFAULT_HASH_KEY_IPv4_ADDR/DEFAULT_HASH_KEY_L4_PORT (0x0A0A0A0A/0x0B0B0B0B) inside the `if (scheme->use_hashing)` branch -- an unrelated mainline RSS-hashing-fallback mechanism. Live-read on .185 scheme 4 confirmed an exact byte-for-byte match. This project's own EKFC override never reprograms these registers, so both existing PORT_ID board measurements (the 2026-07-13 184,320-candidate brute force and the 2026-08-07 16-candidate 0x00-0x0f sweep) were run against this uncontrolled value -- neither result can be trusted to rule the mechanism out. Fix: zero kgse_dv0/kgse_dv1/kgse_ekdv whenever this project's own EKFC override (scheme->ekfc) is in control, so any PORT_ID extraction reads a known 0x00 instead of a leftover RSS constant, making a portid=0x00 retest genuinely controlled for the first time. Dry-run tested (including idempotency) against the exact reconstructed source text before commit.
active.F_181.py: fman_pcd.c: F-181 (2026-08-11) -- source-grounded FE-VM ehash fault-vs-vendor fix.  Compared our fman_pcd_ehash_add_key DDR record to the vendor's genuine ExternalHashTableAddKey() (we-are-mono/ASK 010-ask-fman-dpaa-ehash.patch line 6786) on the running .106 OpenWrt cdx.  Container is bit-identical (en_exthash_bucket {u64 h; pad} + en_ehash_entry).  The ONE delta: the vendor's en_ehash_entry flags u16@0 carries SET_OPC_OFFSET/SET_PARAM_OFFSET pointing to an inline opcode list (terminal ENQUEUE_PKT=0x01) + en_ehash_enqueue_param {mtu u16be, hdr u8, bpid u8, fqid u32be, word, word2} with the flow's TX FQ.  We wrote flags=STATS_EN(0x1000) only and key+u32-ENQ-offset with no opcode-script, so on a HIT the FE-VM walks opc_offset=0 (the header bytes) -> cannot ENQUEUE -> the comparator never completes a HIT (the bracketed zero-HIT fault).  F-181 writes the vendor opcode-script + enqueue_param inline after the key, with flags opc/param offsets computed per the vendor bit packing.  No container change -- 16B bucket/ExternalHashTableAddKey path preserved. Enables the first single-variable HIT test with a genuinely walked action script.
active.F_182.py: fman_pcd.c: F-182 (2026-08-12, E20 corrected track step 1) -- three ehash DDR record bug fixes found in F-181's first silicon test record dump (@0x81c42000): (1) F-175's per-flow ctx pointer write (8B be64 at 8+align8(keysize)) CLOBBERED F-181's opcode slot (8+ALIGN(keysize,4)) -- both = 24 for keysize 14; dump showed opcode[24]=0x00 under the ctx_dma be64. Relocated the ctx pointer past the opcode area + param block (offset 56 for keysize 14, 80 for the 37B IPv6 key; inside the 256B record, past everything the FE-VM walks). (2) param.fqid carried the ENQ FE MURAM offset (dump [44..47]=0x00055f00) -- vendor writes the flow's actual target FQID there (cdx create_enque_hm: param->fqid = cpu_to_be32(l2_info.fqid)). Now writes the add_key fqid parameter. (3) Cleared SET_STATS_ENABLE -- vendor sets it only with the 320B ext entry (stats at +256) + UPDATE_STATS in the hashfe word; we have neither, so the bit could only be inert-or-overflow; pkt_count was never a valid discriminator (E20 confound #3; M3 gate = fe_obs canary, patch 0169). active.F_186.py: fman_pcd.c/fman_pcd_kg.c: F-186 (2026-08-12, E25 silicon-proof, .185 6.18.44-vyos, live /dev/mem validated) -- correct the F-185 node miss-action. E24/E25 proved the F-185 miss form (miss_action_type=NIA, word0 bits[31:30]=0b01, word3 = KG|DIRECT|CC_EN|scheme NIA) is FATAL on the 210.10.1 blob: empty-bucket MISS -> word3 NIA -> full KG re-classification into the AC_CC scheme -> node -> MISS -> NIA = INFINITE LOOP (spc ~4.5M classifications/sec sustained for minutes, no hop limit, no stall, frames never terminate; recovery = fe_arm disengage); KG-direct to a FOREIGN scheme instead -> FM_FD_ERR_NO_SCHEME (0x00004000) -> port error FQ 0x291 (dmesg 'Err FD status = 0x00004000'). E25 also proved the miss fqid MUST be the frame's own-port base fqid: cross-port fqb (0x200/eth3) delivers to eth3's FQ but the dpaa driver drops it (eth3 rx_dropped++; the FD's buffer belongs to the frame's own BM pool). 2 blocks: (1) fman_pcd.c engage node word0 -> (2U<<30) ENQUE (fallback RM group untouched); (2) fman_pcd_kg.c arm_fe captures u32 miss_fqid = slot->base_fqid under the lock (before mutex_unlock) and commits it as node word3 via fman_pcd_fe_node_set_miss_nia(pcd, fe_enter_off, miss_fqid) instead of the KG-direct NIA -- lands before fman_port_set_cc_base() asserts EXTC SYNC. bpid INTENTIONALLY NOT changed (record keeps bpid=0): bpid=0 to the own-port fqb was never cleanly tested in E25 (all bpid=1 HIT runs were live /dev/mem patches), so whether the machine uses the record's param.bpid on the ENQUEUE_PKT path is an open single-variable E26 matrix test; if it matters it becomes F-187. active.F_187.py: fman_pcd.c: F-187 (2026-08-12, E26 follow-up) -- free the fe_hashfe miss-result allocations on hash free. fman_pcd_fe_hash_build() allocates per successful build: pcd->miss_res_off = fman_pcd_muram_alloc(pcd, 16) (16 B MURAM t_ExtHashResult) + pcd->miss_ctx = dma_alloc_coherent(dev, 256, ...) (256 B DDR), writing the missResult pointer into the hash FE AD w4. fman_pcd_fe_hash_free() returned ONLY the FE object to the fe_available pool and cleared fe_hash_off -- it never freed miss_res_off or miss_ctx. Measured on .185 (6.18.44-vyos, muram_budget debugfs): exactly +16 B MURAM per fe_hashfe build/clear cycle, perfectly linear (1616 -> 1632 -> 1648 -> 1664 across clean cycles; +80 B total across the E26 session = 16 x 5 hash builds; the 256 B DMA context leaks alongside, invisible to the MURAM budget). The minimal arm (no hashfe build) leaks 0, isolating the defect to this pair. The hash FE is part of the legacy MURAM FE chain (the node dispatch does not use it), so production impact is minimal, but the leak violates the pcd-snapshot 'used MUST return to baseline' reversibility invariant and leaks 256 B DMA per cycle. FIX (1 block): in fman_pcd_fe_hash_free(), after the FE object is returned to the pool, free miss_res_off (fman_pcd_muram_free, 16 B) and miss_ctx (dma_free_coherent via list_last_entry_or_null(&pcd->fe_ehash_tables, ...)->dev -- the same lookup the build uses), resetting both to 0/NULL, guarded on non-zero/NULL so a no-op path cannot double-free. The hash AD was already zeroed (FMAN_PCD_FE_MAX_SIZE memset) so the missResult pointer reference is gone before freeing the target. Anchored on the exact post-F-186 fe_hash_free tail; runs after F-186.

active.F_214.py: fman_keygen.c/internal.h/fman_pcd_kg.c: F-214 (2026-08-19, gated) keygen_cls_plan0_passall writes global classification-plan group0=0xffffffff ONCE (keygen->cls_plan0_passall flag set after readback; later port engages skip all AR access) so QLCV carries parser LCV; one-time rule fixes second-port FMFP_EXTC SYNC timeout from rewriting shared CP group while first port live; wired into F-211 v6 arm; default-OFF
active.F_215.py: fman.h/fman.c/fman_port.c: F-215 gate the global FMFP_EXTC[INV0] SYNC (F-168) to fire ONLY for the first engaged RX port via a per-FMan cc_engaged_ports counter; a live sibling keeps the FMan controller non-quiescent so the 2nd-port INV0 never clears -> multi-port arm wedge (image 2040/2129). Fixes IPv4+IPv6 multi-port arm; matches vendor (no INV0 on arm with siblings live)
active.F_216.py: drivers/net/ethernet/freescale/dpaa/dpaa_eth.c: F-216 add ratelimited zero-address FD guard before dma_unmap/phys_to_virt/headroom reads (logs status/format/BPID/offset/length/FQID, consumes without release), and remove obsolete F-072/F-170 be64 frame-data hash capture + normalize RXHASH braces. Image 2228 panic: addr=0 -> phys_to_virt(0)+hash_offset0x108 fault. Defensive/logging, not root malformed-FD fix.
active.F_218.py: fman_pcd.c: F-218 (T-M6-1) fman_pcd_fe_flow_del selects ehash table by key_size (38-byte v6 key -> table1, else table0) so v6 FLOW_CLS_DESTROY unlinks the table1 record instead of leaking; no ABI change; v4 byte-identical
active.F_234_frag.py: fman_pcd.c: F-234 (T-M6-8) VLAN L2-rebuild frag context. Lazily allocates+inits a cdx-style cdx_ucode_frag_info_t (24B, frag_options=BPID_ENABLE|OPT_COUNTER_EN=0x000c, v6_identification=1) in MURAM once, and writes bpid (from the egress port's seeded DPAA RX pool, threaded via ask.ko action.frag_bpid) + word2 (the MURAM frag-block offset, filled kernel-side by fman_pcd_get_frag_muram_off) into the ENQUEUE param of VLAN records ONLY. Gated on vlan->flags && frag_bpid && frag_muram_off; routed/NAT records keep bpid=0/word2=0 -> byte-identical. Fixes the ~20-packet VLAN offload freeze (FE-VM STRIP_ETH+INSERT_L2 rebuild-buffer starvation). Runs after F-233.
